Article Title: Vote chori protest: Gaurav Gogoi, other Congress leaders detained; cops use water cannons in Patna, Chandigarh
Article Text:
Water cannons used on Congress protesters in Chandigarh, Patna

Protests spread across states

CJP threatens nationwide protests

Youth Congress launches online petition

Rahul Gandhi steps up allegations

Priyanka backs Rahul’s allegations

ECI rejects claims of internal dissent

Chirag Paswan asks ECI to clarify

SC plea challenges Gyanesh Kumar

NEW DELHI: Assam Congress chief Gaurav Gogoi and several party leaders were detained during a protest in Guwahati on Friday demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The detentions came as Congress workers staged demonstrations in several states over the functioning of the Election Commission.The Jantar mantar protest site has been closed for protestors whereas police used water cannons to disperse protesters in Chandigarh and Patna during the demonstrations.Security personnel were also deployed outside the Election Commission office in New Delhi ahead of a Delhi Congress demonstration over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The Indian Youth Congress was also scheduled to march from Raisina Road to Jantar Mantar.The protests follow an Indian Express report that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders related to the SIR process. The report said their concerns included voter registration, deletion and restoration of names and access to electoral-roll databases.The Madhya Pradesh Youth Congress held a protest outside the Chief Electoral Officer’s office in Bhopal on Thursday, demanding Kumar’s resignation. Protesters raised slogans against the CEC and carried posters reading “arrest Gyanesh Kumar for treason” and “Vote-Chori magic trick exposed”.In Dehradun, Congress workers also staged a protest demanding Kumar’s resignation, with Congress MP Kumari Selja leading the demonstration.In Punjab, Pradesh Congress Committee president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring demanded Kumar’s dismissal, an FIR against him and his alleged collaborators, and their arrest. He also announced a march to the ECI office in Chandigarh under the leadership of Sachin Pilot.In Karnataka, the Pradesh Congress Committee filed a police complaint seeking action against Kumar and BJP MLA Abhay Patil over alleged violations of voting rights and alleged attempts to manipulate electoral rolls. Congress alleged that Patil had sought deletion of eligible voters’ names and sought penal action against Kumar over alleged arbitrary deletions.Congress workers in Kolkata, West Bengal also staged a protest demanding the resignation of Kumar.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke on Friday said his organisation would launch nationwide protests from October 2 if Kumar did not resign by Saturday.In a post on X, Dipke said CJP would begin its protest from Mumbai on Gandhi Jayanti and subsequently take the agitation to cities across India.“If Gyanesh Kumar does not resign by tomorrow, CJP will begin its nationwide protest from Mumbai on 2 October, and take it to cities across India. This Gandhi Jayanti let’s pledge to save democracy,” Dipke wrote.The announcement came a day after Dipke demanded Kumar’s resignation and threatened a “Jantar Mantar 2.0” agitation if his demand was not met.The Indian Youth Congress on Thursday launched a nationwide online citizens’ petition titled “Gyanesh, It’s Done Bro”, seeking action against Kumar and urging citizens, particularly young people, to participate in a campaign for electoral transparency and accountability.The IYC has demanded Kumar’s removal as CEC, along with his arrest and prosecution. It has also sought a comprehensive investigation into electoral-roll processes, the alleged BJP connection raised by the campaign, and the release of electoral records and internal objections.Opposition plans removal motionOpposition parties are also preparing to move a motion seeking Kumar’s removal in both Houses of Parliament, with Congress reaching out to other opposition parties, party sources said. The notice is expected to be submitted in the coming days. A similar move is being prepared as the political dispute over the ECI and SIR continues.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Thursday alleged with “100 per cent certainty” that elections in India, including the 2024 Lok Sabha polls and several Assembly contests, had been “rigged”. He demanded Kumar’s resignation and alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah were at the top of a conspiracy and would face investigation.“The first thing we are saying is Mr. Gyanesh Kumar must resign immediately... This thing that you have done is an act against the Indian nation... A person who attacks the vote, who fundamentally destroys India's democratic institution, is nothing other than a 'Desh Drohi',” Gandhi said.He also said the CEC should “turn Approver”.In Raipur, All India Adivasi Congress president Vikrant Bhuria defended Gandhi’s allegations of “vote theft”, saying they were based on facts.“Whatever Rahul Gandhi says is based on facts, and history bears witness that every claim he has made has eventually been proven true. We had been campaigning for quite some time, under his leadership, against vote theft, highlighting that votes were being stolen, elections were being rigged, names were being deleted from voter lists, and the names of ineligible people were being added,” Bhuria told ANI.“Instances were found where thousands of voters were registered at a single address. He substantiated these claims with facts, yet the Election Commission failed to take cognizance of them,” he added.Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra defended Rahul Gandhi’s allegations and rejected the BJP’s response to the controversy.“I'm sorry, that's a very stale and weak story. There are facts, there is evidence. It is there for the whole country to see. My brother (Rahul Gandhi) has shown it in many different press conferences. He has put the evidence forward. Now it is very clear. 13 crore voters have been deleted. This is a lame excuse, and the BJP should stop making lame excuses. If they are meddling with our elections and if their leadership is making the Election Commission do this, then it is an act of treason and they should be aware of it. ..They are doing an illegal act. How many years has it been that they have been rigging elections? Naturally, they are so overconfident all the time...”Asked whether Congress was planning a protest, she said, “There is a CWC meeting, I think, for which I am having to go back. So they will decide on that meeting and suppose what the course of action will be.”The Election Commission has rejected the assertion that objections raised by Sandhu and Joshi represented structural or institutional dissent over final decisions. The poll panel has said operational queries, internal feedback and administrative suggestions raised during the drafting process are part of the normal functioning of a multi-member constitutional body. It has maintained that all final decisions, including those related to SIR, were unanimous.The ECI has also said ECINet is a secure, decentralised digital platform operated under the Representation of the People Acts, 1950 and 1951. According to the poll panel, statutory duties on the platform are carried out by designated field officers, including BLOs, AEROs, EROs, DEOs and CEOs, using unique IDs and secure credentials.Union minister Chirag Paswan said that if questions are being raised about the Election Commission, an independent constitutional body, the responsibility lies with the CEC to present his position clearly.“If questions are being raised on Election Commission, which is an independent constitutional body, responsibility lies with CEC to present his stance clearly. It is problematic if people begin to doubt electoral process itself. EC needs to present its stance, not to Rahul Gandhi, but to public,” Paswan said.The controversy over the SIR exercise and the ECI’s internal functioning is expected to be taken up at the Congress Working Committee meeting scheduled for September 29 in New Delhi.A plea filed in the Supreme Court has challenged alleged unilateral decisions taken by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in connection with the Election Commission’s electoral-roll revision exercise, including the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).The petitioner has sought an SIT investigation into the alleged deletion of around 13 crore voters from electoral rolls. The plea also seeks a declaration that decisions allegedly taken without the concurrence of the other two Election Commissioners were illegal.It has further sought restoration of the original Form 6 used for voter registration and prosecution of Gyanesh Kumar, Deputy Election Commissioner Maneesh Garg and ECI IT head Seema Khanna for alleged violations of their duties under the Representation of the People Act.
Article Summary: Water cannons used on Congress protesters in Chandigarh, Patna. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke threatens nationwide protests if Gyanesh Kumar does not resign by Saturday. Opposition parties preparing to move motion seeking Kumar’s removal in both Houses of Parliament.

Article Title: 'No anti-incumbency against BJP?' Party counters Rahul Gandhi with Tamil Nadu, Bengal poll history
Article Text:
BJP counters Rahul Gandhi with Tamil Nadu, Bengal poll history

What Rahul Gandhi said

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi 's claim that anti-incumbency has “disappeared” for the BJP because of its alleged collusion with the Election Commission drew a sharp response from the ruling party. BJP national spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi cited the Congress's electoral record in states including Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Odisha to hit back at leader of opposition in Lok Sabha.Rahul Gandhi, speaking at a press conference in New Delhi on Thursday amid the ongoing row over the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, questioned how anti-incumbency could seemingly affect successive governments but not the BJP.Responding to Rahul's remarks, BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi questioned his understanding of Indian electoral history and argued that the stronger long-term anti-incumbency trend was against the Congress."From a political point of view, his wisdom is zero, his knowledge is zero," Trivedi said, launching a personal attack on Rahul.Trivedi then pointed to states where the Congress has not returned to power for decades."Yes, anti-incumbency is indeed very strong and consistent against Congress," he said.On Tamil Nadu, Trivedi said the Congress had not returned to power since 1967, arguing that the BJP was not even a significant political force in the state at the time. In West Bengal, he said, the Congress had not returned to government since 1977.The Election Commission's statistical reports list assembly elections across the states and provide the historical electoral data on which such comparisons can be made.The BJP spokesperson also cited Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Odisha, saying there had been no Congress government in Bihar after 1990, no Congress government in Uttar Pradesh after 1989 and no Congress government in Odisha since 1999."Ever since transparent elections have taken place, CCTV cameras have come in, and independent media has arrived, they've started finding it difficult to come to power," Trivedi said.Earlier in the day, Rahul held a press conference in which he cited former PM Indira Gandhi as an example, saying she was at the height of her popularity after the 1971 Bangladesh war but faced "massive anti-incumbency" within a year or two."The same thing happens to leader after leader, to Congress leaders and to regional parties. But, for some reason, it does not happen to PM Modi, Amit Shah and the BJP," Rahul Gandhi said.He also pointed to electoral changes in Haryana, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh, arguing that these states had historically seen voters shift between parties."Haryana swings from one party to another for 50 years, but suddenly anti-incumbency disappears. Maharashtra swings; suddenly that disappears. Uttar Pradesh swings, from the Samajwadi Party to the Bahujan Samaj Party, that also disappears," he said.Rahul said the question had been a "fundamental" one for the Congress until the party arrived at what he described as the answer: "vote chori".His remarks came as he stepped up his attack on the Election Commission over the SIR exercise. He accused chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of undermining the electoral process, demanded his resignation and alleged that the destruction of votes would ultimately undermine the Constitution and institutions."From vote chori comes kanoon chori, and from that comes sanstha chori," he said.
Article Summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi claims anti-incumbency has "disappeared" for the BJP because of its alleged collusion with the Election Commission. BJP national spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi cited the Congress's electoral record in states including Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Odisha to hit back.

Article Title: 'Allow arrested Congress candidate to contest Nandigram bypoll': HC's oral direction to West Bengal govt
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Calcutta high court on Thursday orally directed the West Bengal government to allow arrested Congress candidate Milan Pradhan to contest the upcoming Nandigram assembly bypoll.Justice Saugata Bhattacharya held that Pradhan would not be treated as "arrested" in the 2007 case for which a lower court remanded him to judicial custody until October 7.Pradhan had challenged his arrest in the case, which was not among the 11 cases mentioned before the high court on September 22. The court noted that the state had produced no document showing that a production warrant had been served on the Congress candidate.“It is surprising to note that the said criminal prosecution is of 2007 and the investigating officer made a prayer for treating the petitioner as ‘shown arrest’ on September 19,” the court observed.On September 22 too, the bench had orally asked the West Bengal government to allow Pradhan to contest the Nandigram bypoll, subject to his securing bail in the five cases in which he had been arrested.The court noted that Pradhan was shown "arrested" in the Khejuri police station case after the September 22 hearing.Justice Bhattacharyya directed the police not to take any steps against Pradhan until October 12 in case number 45 of 2007 at Khejuri police station in Purba Medinipur district and ordered that he not be treated as arrested in the case.The court questioned why Pradhan had been arraigned in another case after the state had told it that he was not wanted in any other case.Pradhan’s counsel Ayan Bhattacharjee told the bench he was "unaware" of the Khejuri case and that the prosecution had not disclosed the production warrant to the high court.Additional advocate general Rajdeep Majumdar, appearing for the state, said the Contai ACJM court had issued the warrant on September 19. Pradhan faces charges including murder and attempt to murder in the case.The cases against Pradhan stem from protests against land acquisition by the then Left Front government in Nandigram and Khejuri in 2007. Police said the pending cases include charges of murder, attempt to murder, abduction with intent to murder, rioting with arms and offences under the Arms Act.He has filed bail applications in four cases.Pradhan was arrested on September 18, hours after Mamata Banerjee announced that her Trinamool Congress faction would support him after its candidate, Sanchita Pradhan De, withdrew from the Nandigram contest.The Nandigram seat fell vacant after West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari retained Bhabanipur, Mamata Banerjee’s erstwhile stronghold. The bypoll will be held on October 6, with counting on October 9.
Article Summary: The Calcutta high court orally directed the West Bengal government to allow arrested Congress candidate Milan Pradhan to contest the upcoming Nandigram assembly bypoll. Justice Saugata Bhattacharya held that Prdhan would not be treated as "arrested" in the 2007 case for which a lower court remanded him to judicial custody until October 7.

Article Title: Delhi HC denies anticipatory bail to YouTuber Ajeet Bharti in casteist remarks case

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court on Thursday refused to grant anticipatory bail to YouTuber Ajeet Bharti in a case over alleged casteist and derogatory remarks against Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad, holding that the plea was not maintainable.Justice Saurabh Banerjee dismissed Bharti’s pre-arrest bail plea, saying a case under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act was prima facie made out against him. The court also noted the statutory bar on granting anticipatory bail under the Act."In view of the fact that a case under the provisions of the SC/ST Act is prima facie made out against the applicant and considering the statutory bar (on grant of bail) under the SC/ST Act, the present petition seeking grant of anticipatory bail is dismissed being not maintainable," the judge said while pronouncing the verdict.The detailed order is awaited.The high court had reserved its order on September 16 after hearing arguments from Bharti's counsel, the Delhi Police and Azad.Bharti had moved the high court after a Delhi trial court rejected his anticipatory bail plea on September 7. The trial court had found that the material before it prima facie disclosed the ingredients of an offence under the SC/ST Act and that the statutory bar on pre-arrest bail applied.Bharti's counsel argued before the high court that the SC/ST Act was not attracted because there was no intentional insult or humiliation. He said the remarks should be considered in the context in which they were made.His lawyer also argued that Bharti had not used any casteist slur and had made the remarks during an exchange on social media after what he described as serious provocation involving a family member.The Delhi Police opposed the plea, arguing that the words allegedly used by Bharti directly insulted a particular caste. The prosecutor said the remarks were made on a social media platform and not in a closed setting, and contended that the ingredients required to attract the SC/ST Act were present.Azad's lawyer also opposed the anticipatory bail plea, describing the alleged remarks as derogatory and intentional.Azad, the Bhim Army chief, had complained to the Delhi Police that Bharti made caste-based, abusive, derogatory and humiliating statements against him, members of the Scheduled Caste community and B R Ambedkar on social media.The FIR was registered under provisions of the SC/ST Act, the Information Technology Act and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The case relates to remarks allegedly made by Bharti during a programme on social media. The complaint was registered at Delhi's North Avenue police station.Bharti had challenged the September 7 trial court order, arguing that the allegations did not make out an offence under the SC/ST Act and that custodial interrogation was not required since the material forming the basis of the case was already available in the public domain.The trial court had said its observations were limited to deciding the anticipatory bail plea and did not amount to an opinion on the merits of the case.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court dismisses YouTuber Ajeet Bharti’s anticipatory bail plea in caste remarks case. Bhim Army chief Chandrashekhar Azad had complained to the Delhi Police that Bh Barti made caste-based, abusive, derogatory and humiliating statements against him, members of the Scheduled Caste community and B R Ambedkar.

Article Title: 9 dead after moving bus catches fire on Yamuna Expressway near Noida airport
Article Text:
A passenger bus caught fire on the Yamuna Expressway

NOIDA: Nine passengers were killed after a private bus travelling from Delhi to Mahoba caught fire on the Yamuna Expressway near Jewar late Wednesday night.Several other passengers sustained burn injuries and were rushed to Kailash Hospital in Jewar, officials said.The incident occurred around 11.30pm near kilometre 33 of the Yamuna Expressway, when the bus, operated by Raj Kalpana Travels, was travelling from Delhi towards Agra. The complainant, Sunil Kumar, a resident of Hamirpur, told police that around 30-35 passengers were travelling in the bus.According to the complaint, passengers began noticing a burning smell coming from the driver's cabin. They allegedly informed the driver and conductor about it, but the two did not stop the bus or inspect the suspected source of the smell. The complaint further alleged that the driver and conductor continued smoking inside the cabin and dismissed the passengers' concerns, saying that such a smell was common in the bus.A short while later, flames suddenly erupted near the driver's seat and rapidly spread through the vehicle. Passengers raised an alarm and repeatedly asked the driver to stop the bus, but the driver allegedly failed to act immediately.As the fire intensified, smoke filled the passenger compartment, leaving several people trapped inside. Sunil and some other passengers managed to escape by jumping out of the bus after it stopped. Several others, however, were unable to get out because of the flames and thick smoke.The injured passengers were taken to Kailash Hospital in Jewar for treatment. On reaching the hospital, the complainant was informed that doctors had declared nine people dead.The complaint also stated that passengers' bags, mobile phones and other belongings were destroyed in the fire. Luggage kept in the bus's luggage compartment and on its roof was also burnt.Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced an ex-gratia of Rs 2 lakh each from the PM National Relief Fund for the next of kin of the nine deceased and Rs 50,000 for each injured person.Expressing grief over the incident, Modi said he was "distressed" by the loss of lives and prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured.President Droupadi Murmu also expressed grief over the deaths and extended condolences to the families of the victims. Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath had earlier announced financial assistance of Rs 2 lakh each for the families of the deceased and Rs 50,000 each for the injured.Police have registered a case based on the complaint and initiated an investigation. The identities of the deceased and the exact cause of the fire are yet to be officially ascertained. Police are also expected to examine the bus, statements of survivors and other evidence to determine how the fire started and whether safety precautions were ignored.
Article Summary: The bus was travelling from Delhi to Mahoba when it caught fire. Passengers raised an alarm and repeatedly asked the driver to stop the bus. Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced an ex-gratia of Rs 2 lakh each from the PM National Relief Fund for the next of kin.

Article Title: BJP defends EC, says oppn trying to discredit panel

NEW DELHI: Differences of opinion within EC are a sign of its democratic functioning, BJP said Wednesday as it mounted a strong counter-charge against the Opposition over its attack on the poll body and govt, saying its rivals have been trying to discredit institutions since 2014, including before the rollout of SIR, due to their dwindling popular support."If there is no discussion of any kind among three election commissioners and they simply agree to everything, then these very opposition parties will call it dictatorship and claim that they were all 'yes men' because they were appointed by govt," BJP's Sambit Patra said.Now, the media has reported their correspondences as a divergence of views on the appropriateness of some measures taken by the commission, and this is a sign of a healthy democracy, he added.Targeting the Opposition for its allegation that BJP's impressive run of recent poll victories was aided by SIR, he said, "The statistics from Bengal expose the Opposition's narrative of 'vote chori', as TMC won 13 of the 20 seats with the highest number of deleted voters, while BJP won only six." Opposition's outrage is an outcome of its receding influence since 2014, when PM Modi led NDA to a huge victory, he said.BJP also cited alleged links of several past ECs, including ex-CECs M S Gill and Navin Chawla, to Congress during its long stint in office.

Article Title: 'We don't smoke at all': Drivers accused in Noida bus fire deny smoking inside vehicle
Article Text:
2 bus drivers and a conductor arrested in Greater Noida bus fire case (Photo credit: X)





GREATER NOIDA: The two drivers arrested in connection with the Greater Noida sleeper bus fire on Thursday denied police allegations that they had been smoking inside the bus before the blaze, saying, “No, this is wrong. We don't smoke at all.”The accused drivers and a conductor were produced before the District and Sessions Court in Surajpur on Thursday and were sent to 14-day judicial custody.The three were arrested in connection with the sleeper bus fire, which claimed nine lives and left several others injured. Police had alleged that the two drivers were smoking inside the bus before the incident.However, the drivers denied the allegation while being taken to court.The police investigation into the circumstances leading to the fire is underway.Meanwhile, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced an ex-gratia of Rs 2 lakh each from the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund for the next of kin of those who died in the fire. Each injured person will receive Rs 50,000.Prime Minister Modi expressed condolences to the families of those killed and wished the injured a speedy recovery.Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has also announced Rs 2 lakh for the family of each deceased victim and Rs 50,000 for each injured person.
Article Summary: The two drivers denied police allegations that they had been smoking inside the bus before the blaze. The accused drivers and a conductor were produced before the District and Sessions Court in Surajpur on Thursday. The three were arrested in connection with the Greater Noida sleeper bus fire, which claimed nine lives and left several others injured.

KOLKATA: Calcutta High Court on Thursday pulled up Election Commission for allotting ‘envelope’ symbol — used by Indian Secular Front in the 2026 assembly election — to Democratic Trinamool Congress for the Oct 6 bypoll, and berated the commission for “creating trouble” and forcing parties to start legal proceedings thereby “burdening” the court.“Really fed up with the authority.... Once the elections start, you start creating trouble. Then parties come to court, putting burden on the court,” the high court told EC’s counsel.“Authorities should act impartially and fairly,” Justice Krishna Rao told the poll panel and questioned why it had to choose ‘envelope’ from among 183 symbols to give to another party. The angry judge asked why EC was getting into disputes and ruffling parties to create legal proceedings. “Is this the way it works?” he asked.Nawsad Siddiqui-led ISF, which won the Bhangar seat in assembly elections, had moved the high court praying for a direction to EC to freeze the ‘envelope’ symbol. After allotting ‘envelope’ to Democratic Trinamool Congress, EC gave ISF the ‘almirah’ symbol for the bypolls.“Our voters will be confused. We fought the 2026 assembly election using ‘envelope’ and we are also contesting the bypolls,” ISF’s counsel and senior advocate Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharyya told the judge.EC’s counsel argued that ISF is a registered unrecognised party and such parties do not have reserved symbols. ISF was given ‘envelope’ twice, the last being the 2026 assembly election. ISF countered that the by-election was a continuation of the assembly election.When Justice Rao asked if ISF had applied for a symbol for the bypoll, its counsel said there was no new notification asking political parties to submit Form 10b for allotment of symbols.Justice Rao said, “If you (EC) find that just four months back the symbol was used by one political party, for the by-election why did you choose that particular symbol? You could have kept it reserved like the others. Why did you not keep it reserved?”The matter will be heard again on Friday.
Article Summary: Calcutta High Court expressed frustration at the Election Commission for assigning the 'envelope' symbol to a different party. Indian Secular Front won the Bhangar seat in assembly elections, had moved the high court praying for a direction to EC to freeze the ‘en envelope’ symbol.

Article Title: ‘CJP leaders carried out cyber-assault’: Delhi HC to hear woman’s plea over deepfake photo with PM Modi
Article Text:
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, centre, addresses a press conference as co-conveners Saurav Das, left and Ashutosh Ranka.





NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Friday allowed urgent listing of a plea seeking directions to four Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders to remove an alleged deepfake image of a woman alongside Prime Minister Narendra Modi from social media, according to LiveLaw.The plea names CJP leaders Saurav Das, Abhijit Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Ratna Singh as respondents.The matter was mentioned before a division bench comprising Chief Justice DK Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia, which directed that it be listed on Friday.The woman, identified as Riddhima Sharma in the complaint, has alleged that the CJP leaders carried out a coordinated cyber-assault and publicly targeted her using a morphed image.According to LiveLaw, the leaders allegedly used her photograph without permission and employed AI face-swapping tools to superimpose her face on what she described as a "highly vulgar and compromising image" alongside Modi.The complaint relates to a protest organised by the CJP at Jantar Mantar, where the alleged morphed image was displayed, according to the plea.Delhi Police registered an FIR at the Cyber police station in New Delhi on Thursday following the woman's complaint. The case has been registered under relevant provisions of the Information Technology Act and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The plea has sought directions for the removal of the alleged deepfake image from social media platforms and other online sources.The allegations are part of the woman's complaint and have not been established by the court.
Article Summary: The Delhi high court allowed urgent listing of a plea seeking directions to four Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders to remove an alleged deepfake image. The plea names CJP leaders Saurav Das, Abhijit Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Ratna Singh as respondents. The woman, identified as Riddhima Sharma in the complaint, has alleged that the leaders carried out a coordinated cyber-assault.

Article Title: ​Conman spins fake accident tale, dupes Beed official of Rs 30,000
Article Text:
TOI

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





A fraudster allegedly took the sub-divisional officer of Majalgaon, in Beed, for a ride with an elaborate tale about the Mumbai collector’s son meeting with an accident. He claimed the injured man urgently needed an ambulance and money for hospitalisation.And the story came with just enough official-sounding backing to make it convincing. Majalgaon Rural police station in-charge Vijay Ramod said the fraudster first contacted the personal assistant of a former minister from Beed and sought “help”.“The PA then called the sub-divisional officer (SDO) and alerted him about the claimed accident in his jurisdiction. Soon, the fraudster contacted the SDOand asked for the money,” Ramod said.Two calls in quick succession did the trick. With little time to verify the story, the officer asked his brother to arrange for Rs 30,000.The money was paid immediately. Soon, however, doubts crept in.“After a few hours, the SDObecame suspicious. He contacted the Beed district collector to verify the alleged accident and learnt that no such incident had taken place,” Ramod said. By then, however, the conman had disappeared.Beed Rural police registered a case under BNS section 318(2) for cheating on Sept 21. Further investigation is underway..
Article Summary: A fraudster allegedly took the sub-divisional officer of Majalgaon, in Beed, for a ride with an elaborate tale. He claimed the injured man urgently needed an ambulance and money for hospitalisation. With little time to verify the story, the officer asked his brother to arrange for Rs 30,000.

Article Title: Uddhav should stop blaming ECI for his defeats: CM
Article Text:
CM Devendra Fadnavis

Kolhapur:





Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray should stop blaming Election Commission of India (ECI) ECI for his defeats and Mahayuti’s win in Maharashtra , chief minister Devendra Fadnavis said on Wednesday while speaking in Solapur.Asked about Thackeray’s demand for re-elections in Maharashtra and other states over ECI row, Fadnavis called it futile, citing the idiom: “The wound is on the forehead, but the bandage is tied to the knee”.“Why did he lose, why did people reject him? Instead of researching this, he only does one thing, that is, blaming the ECI. If Congress wins Telangana then ECI is doing a good job; if Congress wins Karnataka then ECI is good. But it is bad when Mahayuti wins in Maharashtra. This should stop,” Fadnavis said while speaking to the reporters in Solapur during a field visit to gauge the crop loss situation amid severe water scarcity.Addressing a news conference on Wednesday, Thackeray demanded sacking of chief election commissioner Dyanesh Kumar over alleged objections by the other two election commissioners.Lakhs of voters were added post-Lok Sabha election in Maharashtra suspiciously for the assembly election, which, according to him, led to Maha Vikas Aghadi’s defeat.The ECI, however, has denied the allegations. Thackeray said that Kumar’s conduct should also be probed.
Article Summary: Uddhav Thackeray should stop blaming Election Commission of India (ECI) ECI for his defeats and Mahayuti’s win in Maharashtra, chief minister Devendra Fadnavis said on Wednesday. “Why did he lose, why did people reject him? Instead of researching this, he only does one thing, that is, blaming the ECI. This should stop,” he said.

Article Title: Cops on Ganpati patrol hit by speeding MUV on Thane-Belapur Road, driver flees
Article Text:
The incident took place near Digha pond on the Belapur-bound lane at around 12.20am on Monday.





NAVI MUMBAI: In a hit-and-run incident on the Thane-Belapur Road, a police constable and a woman assistant sub-inspector (ASI) were injured when a speeding MUV rammed into their motorcycle from behind while they were patrolling during the seventh day of Ganpati immersion.The incident took place near Digha pond on the Belapur-bound lane at around 12.20am on Monday.The injured cops were identified as constable Umesh Patil, 41, who was riding his personal motorcycle, and ASI Rashmin Magar, who was riding pillion.The motorcycle skidded after being hit by the MUV. Patil sustained injuries to his left leg, while Magar suffered bruises to her left elbow, shoulder and left leg.Acting on a complaint filed by Patil, Rabale MIDC police registered an FIR under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Motor Vehicles Act against the MUV driver. Police traced him to his residence in Ghansoli.Devidas Kathale, senior inspector of Rabale MIDC police, said, “As the accused MUV driver's wife is due to deliver in a few days, he will be summoned to the police station later and served with a notice under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.”
Article Summary: The incident took place near Digha pond on the Belapur-bound lane at around 12.20am on Monday. The injured cops were identified as constable Umesh Patil, 41, and ASI Rashmin Magar, who was riding pillion. The motorcycle skidded after being hit by the MUV.

Article Title: Speeding SUV hits bike in Vashi, 3 youths injured; driver traced
Article Text:
Accused driver of SUV Mahindra Thar escaping after accident





NAVI MUMBAI: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday.The incident took place around 1am. The injured youths were initially taken to NMMC Hospital in Vashi and were later referred to Sion Hospital for further treatment.Following the incident, a biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police then traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number.During the investigation, it was learnt that the owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride. Police subsequently traced his mobile tower location to an area near the creek in Sector 12, Vashi, where he was allegedly hiding.He was detained and served a notice under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), following which he was released.
Article Summary: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday. A biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number. The owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride.

Article Title: Quack doctor detained in Maharashtra for practising medicine without registration
Article Text:
A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel police after an inspection (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel taluka police after a complaint was lodged by the medical officer of the Primary Health Centre at Ajivali village in Panvel taluka, following an inspection by health department officials at his illegal clinic in Kasalkhand village on Monday afternoon.The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal and resides in an MHADA building in India Bulls Township, Kon village, Panvel.Gajanan Ghadge, senior inspector of Panvel taluka police, informed that the complaint was lodged by medical officer Dr Sayali Mankar, 33, who inspected Haq's clinic in Kasalkhand village and found that he was an unqualified and unregistered medical practitioner allegedly practising modern medicine by posing as a doctor.He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.Inspector Ghadge said, "We have invoked relevant sections of the Maharashtra Medical Practitioners Act, 1961, against the accused, which prohibit any person from practising medicine in the state unless their name is registered under the relevant statutory provisions and prescribe criminal penalties and fines for those who illegally practise medicine without valid registration. Under the law, the accused was served a notice under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), directing him to appear for inquiry when summoned and during the court proceedings. "
Article Summary: The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal. He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.

Article Title: 'Grabbed hand and attempted to disrobe': Cab driver tries to assault woman passenger near Navi Mumbai airport
Article Text:
Police have registered a case and are searching for the accused driver (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver who took the vehicle to a deserted road near Navi Mumbai airport late on Saturday night, police said on Sunday.The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport, police said. The accused allegedly stopped the cab on the pretext of drinking water before moving to the rear seat beside the woman, police said.According to the police, the woman was travelling to Panvel after a friend booked a cab for her following the party."The driver stopped the vehicle on the deserted service road, stepped out briefly, and then re-entered the car, sitting on the rear seat next to the woman. He allegedly grabbed her hand and attempted to disrobe her," said an official of the Navi Mumbai Police.The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.After the incident, the woman contacted her family and went to Panvel Police Station to lodge a complaint.Since the alleged incident took place within the jurisdiction of Navi Mumbai airport police station, Panvel police escorted her to the appropriate police station.Based on her complaint, Navi Mumbai Airport Police registered a case against the accused, identified as Mohammad Afzal Shaikh, under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Police have launched a search for Shaikh and are using technical intelligence to trace his whereabouts.Further investigation is underway.(With ANI inputs)(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)
Article Summary: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver. The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport. The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.

Article Title: PM classmate’s battle for land continues despite BJP MLA's exit, no possession yet
Article Text:
Asgar Ali Vora met the PM on Sept 8 and sought his intervention in the land disp­u­te





BHAYANDAR: Asgar Ali Vora, a schoolmate of Prime Minister Narendra Modi , continues to struggle to regain possession of his land after MLA Narendra Mehta’s company announced that it had relinquished the property. However, another developer is allegedly continuing to retain possession of the land.Vora, 81, had purchased around 2,810 sq m of land at Navghar in Bhayandar East in 1989. He has alleged that Swayam Builders and Mehta’s Seven Eleven Constructions took possession of the property in 2011. After pursuing the matter for nearly 15 years, Vora met PM Modi on Sep 8 and complained against Mehta.Following the meeting, Mehta relinquished possession of the land, while the municipal corporation also cancelled the construction permission granted to him.However, the land has allegedly not been handed back to its original owner. Instead, developers Mukesh Parekh and Mervyn Fernandes are allegedly continuing to retain possession of the property. Following a complaint by Shiv Sena, Navghar police have registered a non-cognisable offence against Seven Eleven Constructions, Parekh and Fernandes.
Article Summary: Asgar Ali Vora, 81, had purchased around 2,810 sq m of land at Navghar in Bhayandar East in 1989. He has alleged that Swayam Builders and Mehta’s Seven Eleven Constructions took possession of the property in 2011. After pursuing the matter for nearly 15 years, Vora met PM Modi on Sep 8 and complained.

Article Title: Maharashtra TET paper leak: 2 key accused arrested; 168 buyers on radar
Article Text:
Two key accused in TET paper leak case arrested

How the leak occured





BHIWANDI: Two key accused allegedly linked to 168 prospective buyers of the leaked Maharashtra Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) question paper have been arrested, nearly two months after police busted the racket, with the SIT now probing the wider network and possible transactions.The two — Pune-based govt employee Prakash Misal and Bihar native Ashok Shaw, who was staying in Delhi — were among the remaining prominent accused identified during the probe. Police said Misal was in touch with around 50 people who had shown interest in buying the paper, while Shaw allegedly maintained a list of 118 prospective buyers. The list was recovered from his Delhi residence.Shaw was arrested in Patna, Bihar, while Misal was arrested near Bhiwandi Naka on Sunday after police learnt he was planning to surrender before a court. Both were produced before the Bhiwandi court and remanded in police custody till Sept 23.The SIT has so far verified 18 of the 118 names on Shaw's list and found they were preparing to appear for the TET examination. Verification of the remaining 100 is underway.Police suspect Shaw was directly linked to Solapur-based coaching-class operator Prakash Pawar, who has already been arrested, and was also in contact with alleged mastermind Bijendra Gupta.Investigators are questioning Misal to determine the price at which he allegedly planned to sell the paper and whether any sale took place. Earlier, accused Kapil Dahiya, who had allegedly travelled to Pune to deliver the paper to Misal, told investigators he could not hand it over.Police had busted the racket two days before the scheduled examination, forcing postponement of the TET.DCP Pawan Bansod confirmed the arrests. ACP Sachin Sangle, part of the SIT, told TOI, "Their interrogation will help us establish to whom they intended to sell the paper."Last week, the SIT filed a 3,470-page chargesheet before the Bhiwandi fast-track court against those arrested earlier in the case.With Misal and Shaw's arrests, police said the two remaining prominent accused identified during the investigation have been apprehended. Further arrests will depend on findings from their contacts and financial transactions.
Article Summary: Pune-based govt employee Prakash Misal and Bihar native Ashok Shaw were among the remaining prominent accused identified during the probe. Police said Misal was in touch with around 50 people who had shown interest in buying the paper. Shaw allegedly maintained a list of 118 prospective buyers.

Article Title: Cong neta seeks protection for 'gangrape' survivor, her kin
Article Text:
(Representative image)





THANE: A day after Padgha police registered an FIR against former Kalyan West MLA Narendra Pawar and dismissed policeman Shailesh Patil for allegedly gangraping a 22-year-old married woman at a farmhouse in Bapgaon, Congress group leader in KDMC Kanchan Kulkarni on Friday sought police protection for the survivor and her family.Kulkarni, who accompanied the woman to the police station, claimed the survivor's life was in danger because of the accused's influence. She urged CM Eknath Shinde to intervene and ensure security for her.Meanwhile, Padgha police conducted a spot panchnama at the farmhouse in Bapgaon to collect forensic evidence. Seperate police teams have also been formed to trace Pawar and Patil, who remain absconding. Pawar has denied the charge, calling them false. He has also resigned from all his BJP organisational posts. - Pradeep Gupta
Article Summary: Congress group leader in KDMC Kanchan Kulkarni sought police protection for the survivor and her family. She urged CM Eknath Shinde to intervene and ensure security for her. Padgha police conducted a spot panchnama at the farmhouse in Bapgaon to collect forensic evidence.

Article Title: Two held with 10kg ganja on private bus near Hosur
Article Text:
The duo had purchased the ganja in bulk from a supplier in Bengaluru and were attempting to transport it to Madurai for resale

Krishnagiri:





Two men were arrested for smuggling 10kg of ganja on a private bus which was heading from Bengaluru to Madurai, in the early hours of Thursday. They were apprehended by the district police during a vehicle check at the Jujuwadi border check post near Hosur.Police officers from the Hosur SIPCOT station were screening vehicles crossing the Tamil Nadu–Karnataka border, when they stopped a ‘Mettur Super Service’ bus bound for Madurai. Special sub-inspector Nagarajan, along with head constables Murugan and Vallal, thoroughly checked passengers’ belongings, during which they found five packets containing 10kg of ganja from two shoulder bags. “The contraband was immediately seized, and the two passengers were detained,” the SSI said.The arrested were subsequently identified as M Sanjay, 24, from Usilampatti, in Madurai district, who is engaged in milk trade, and S Gautham, 34, from Periyakulam, in Theni district, who is employed with a private online delivery company. Preliminary investigation revealed that the duo had purchased the ganja in bulk from a supplier named Rajapandi in Bengaluru’s Madiwala area and were attempting to transport it to Madurai for resale.Both were taken to SIPCOT police station, where a case has been registered. Police have also launched a manhunt for the supplier and are investigating further.
Article Summary: Two men were arrested for smuggling 10kg of ganja on a private bus. They were apprehended by the district police during a vehicle check at the Jujuwadi border check post near Hosur. Police have also launched a manhunt for the supplier and are investigating further.

Article Title: Man booked for harassing woman in Coimbatore
Article Text: COIMBATORE: Race Course police in the city have begun investigations after a 30-year-old married woman lodged a complaint alleging that a man, who is her relative, had repeatedly harassed her sexually.In her complaint, the woman said the 36-year-old man had been frequently speaking to her on the phone. Her husband objected to their conversations and warned her against speaking to her relative.However, the relative continued to contact her on the phone. When she had stopped answering his calls, he contacted her using different phone numbers and harassed her, she stated in her complaint.The woman lodged a complaint with Race Course police on Tuesday. Police registered a case under Section 75 of BNS read with Section 4 of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act.
Article Summary: Married woman alleges that a man, who is her relative, had repeatedly harassed her sexually. The woman said the 36-year-old man had been frequently speaking to her on the phone. Her husband objected to their conversations and warned her against speaking to the relative.

Article Title: Three, including minor held With 18 country-made bombs
Article Text:
Virudhunagar district police arrested three people, including one minor, and confiscated 18 country-made explosives during a routine vehicle check on Wednesday.

Virudhunagar

:





Virudhunagar district police arrested three people, including one minor, and confiscated 18 country-made explosives during a routine vehicle check on Wednesday.The arrested were identified as Manikandan , 18, and Kavirajan, 19, of Watrap, and a 17-year-old minor.Police said a team was conducting a vehicle check on the Watrap-Melapalayam Road near Kannapan Mandapam on Wednesday evening.During the check, police attempted to stop a two-wheeler carrying three people. The trio allegedly tried to evade the police. However, the team intercepted the vehicle.A search of the two-wheeler led to the recovery of 18 country-made explosives.Preliminary inquiries revealed that the trio had allegedly manufactured the explosives themselves and were carrying them for hunting wild animals in the forest area, police said.Watrap police seized the explosives and the two-wheeler. A case was registered under relevant provisions of the Explosive Substances Act. The three were arrested and remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: Virudhunagar district police arrested three people, including one minor, and confiscated 18 country-made explosives during a routine vehicle check on Wednesday. The arrested were identified as Manikandan, 18, and Kavirajan, 19, of Watrap, and a 17-year-old minor.

Article Title: Auto driver arrested for threatening, assaulting cops in Yercaud
Article Text:
Representative image





SALEM: The Yercaud police have arrested an autorickshaw driver on charges of assaulting a special sub-inspector (SSI) and threatening to kill the SSI and a woman police constable.The arrested auto driver has been identified as Yuvraj, 22, of Mundagampadi. Yuvraj, who was drunk, obstructed vehicles near a Vinayagar statue on Monday. Head constable D Thavamani, who was regulating traffic, intervened. Yuvraj abused her verbally.SSI Aaron Athirubaraj attempted to defuse the situation. “But Yuvraj tore my shirt, struck me on the chest and threatened to kill me and Thavamani,” the SSI said.Police registered a case against Yuvraj under sections relating to obstructing govt servants, assault and criminal intimidation. He was remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: The arrested auto driver has been identified as Yuvraj, 22, of Mundagampadi. He was remanded in judicial custody. Police registered a case against him under sections relating to obstructing govt servants, assault and criminal intimidation.

Article Title: Kerala HC moved against govt move in CMRL pay-off case
Article Text:
Kochi:





A petition has been filed in the high court challenging the govt order directing a preliminary police inquiry against former chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan and his kin based on the ED’s recommendation in the CMRL pay-off case, rather than registering a case under the PC Act.The petition filed by K M Shajahan, a social activist and former additional private secretary to late chief minister V S Achuthanandan, will be considered by the court the next day. According to Shajahan, instead of handing over ED’s recommendation to the director of the vigilance and anti-corruption bureau, the state govt issued an order directing a preliminary police inquiry into the matter, which was nothing but “match-fixing” and an attempt to save the alleged culprits. The recommendation made by the ED to the state police chief has now reached the political leadership, the petitioner alleged. Accordingly, a preliminary inquiry by the police was ordered, rather than by the agency exclusively entrusted with offences under the PC Act, he added.Additionally, Shajahan stated in the petition that he had given a complaint to the state police chief (SPC) and vigilance director seeking an investigation into the alleged payments of Rs 3.28 crore made by CMRL to Exalogic Solutions, a defunct company owned by Veena, the daughter of Pinarayi Vijayan, without receiving corresponding IT consultancy services.Meanwhile, ED forwarded the materials collected during its investigation into the matter under the PMLA and recommended that the state police chief register a case against Vijayan, along with his daughter T Veena, son-in-law and former minister P A Mohammed Riyas. Despite an SIT headed by crime branch ADGP H Venkatesh being formed to conduct a preliminary inquiry, no FIR has been registered and no time frame has been prescribed, the petitioner alleged.He further pointed out that, as per the ED’s allegations, Rs 3.28 crore was transferred from CMRL to the former chief minister through his daughter Veena and her company. It was also alleged that illicit funds worth crores of rupees were routed abroad through hawala channels via Mohammed Riyas.
Article Summary: A petition has been filed in the high court challenging the govt order directing a preliminary police inquiry against former chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan. The petition filed by K M Shajahan, a social activist and former additional private secretary to late chief minister V S Achuthanandan, will be considered by the court the next day.

Article Title: Thrissur DIG to probe estate staff’s suicide, says Ramesh Chennithala
Article Text:
Thrissur

:





Home minister Ramesh Chennithala on Thursday said that Thrissur range DIG has been directed to investigate the circumstances that led to the suicide of an employee, Manjusha , at Harrisons Malayalam Ltd in Palappilly.Speaking at a function in Mattathur, the minister also assured that action would be taken against those found guilty. The police would conduct an impartial investigation into the incident, and appropriate steps would be initiated, he said.The body of Manjusha, who was a watcher at the estate company, was found hanging on an electric tower on Tuesday. A suicide note believed to be written by her named some of her superiors as responsible for pushing her to the extreme decision.
Article Summary: Home minister Ramesh Chennithala on Thursday said that Thrissur range DIG has been directed to investigate the circumstances that led to the suicide of an employee. Manjusha, who was a watcher at the estate company, was found hanging on an electric tower. A suicide note believed to be written by her named some of her superiors as responsible for pushing her to the extreme decision.
